entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the applicant, who is the Devar of the deceased,
physically abused the deceased on 20.08.2022, which resulted into the death of the sister of the informant.

3. The Counsel for the applicant argues that the FIR in question was lodged on 21.08.20022 alleging that the deceased was blessed with a daughter, with which, the applicant as unhappy, as such, he caused physical injury, which resulted into the death of the deceased.

It is also argues that the Dinesh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63087286/
1 applicant prior to death used to mental and physical harassment for dowry.
4. The Counsel for the applicant further argues that no postmortem was done over the body of the deceased, as such, there is no evidence so far to implicate the applicant for the offence in question.

entities.text: Dinesh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further drawn my attention that the applicant has a separate family and has blessed with three daughters, as such, there is no reason to tease the deceased on account of birth of a girl child.
He argues that the applicant is in custody since 22.08.2022 and even the charge has not been framed.

The applicant has no criminal antecedents, as such, he should be enlarged on bail.
5.

Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer by arguing that the applicant did not inform any of the relatives and not even his brother or police authority after the death of the deceased and without informing any one, performed the last rituals.
He further argues that the statement of the husband of the deceased is on record, which corroborates the FIR version.
He also relied upon the statements of the neighbours, who stated that the applicant has not good terms with the deceased and used to altercation with the deceased on several occasions.
In the light of the said, he argues that the bail application should be rejected.

6. Considering the submissions made at the bar, prima facie, apart from the statement of the brother of the applicant, nothing on record to demonstrates that the death was on account of unnatural causes, however, it is the subject matter of trial coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 22.08.2022 and even the charge has not been framed, there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
7.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Dinesh be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.467 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 201 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Khairighat, District Bahraich on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
